blocks.text: A percentile is the value below which a given percentage of observations falls. The 25th percentile is the first quartile (Q1), the 50th percentile is the median, and the 75th percentile is the third quartile (Q3). Percentiles help in understanding the distribution of biological data, whether skewed or normally distributed.

The rank of the Pth percentile is R = (P / 100) x (n + 1), where n is the number of observations. If R is a whole number, the percentile is the value at that position in the ordered data; if not, interpolate between the two nearest ranks. For R = 4.4: value = value at 4th + 0.4 x (value at 5th - value at 4th).

Heights (cm) of 10 people: 160, 162, 168, 165, 170, 175, 172, 178, 180, 182. To find the 40th percentile: ordered, 160, 162, 165, 168, 170, 172, 175, 178, 180, 182; n = 10; R = 40 / 100 x (10 + 1) = 4.4, between the 4th (168) and 5th (170) values. Percentile = 168 + 0.4 x (170 - 168) = 168 + 0.8 = 168.8 cm, so 40% of the observations are at or below 168.8 cm.

blocks.prompt: Which percentile is the median, and what are Q1 and Q3?
blocks.explanation: The median is the 50th percentile; Q1 is the 25th and Q3 the 75th percentile.

items: R = (P / 100) x (n + 1); interpolate if R is not whole.
Example: 40th percentile of the heights = 168.8 cm.
